options.label: ~/dev (Recommended)
options.description: Matches the claude supervisor's root and is the broadest scope for the mobile app's file/session view.

options.label: $HOME
options.description: Even broader scope; pairs the relay at the user-home level.

options.label: A specific repo dir
options.description: Constrain the relay to a single project (you'll tell me which).

questions.question: How should the codex-relay supervisor relate to the claude one?

options.label: Separate script + plist (Recommended)
options.description: New codex-relay-supervisor.sh and com.claudio1.codex-relay.plist alongside the claude pair; install.sh installs both. Keeps the two bridges independent — restart one without touching the other.

options.label: Fold into existing supervisor
options.description: Extend remote-control-supervisor.sh to also manage codex-relay. Single process, fewer plists, but couples the two lifecycles and conflates discovery (per-dir claude vs single-instance codex).

transcript_tail.text:
is codex relay ran as a service? if not what is needed to do it?

if a project is needed let add to remote control dir
Let me check what "codex relay" might refer to on this system.
The user clarified — they mean `codex-relay` (the npm package). Let me check it.

No — `codex-relay` ships as a CLI you launch yourself (`npx codex-relay@latest`). It has a `--bg` flag that daemonizes (drops `.codex-relay/server.pid|server.log|server-state.json|auth.db` in the CWD, binds `0.0.0.0:8787`), but **it does not register with launchd**, doesn't survive logout/reboot, and doesn't auto-restart on crash. There's no official launchd/systemd guidance from upstream.

So to run it "as a service" you'd add roughly the same pattern that's already here for `claude remote-control`:

- `codex-relay-supervisor.sh` — keeps one `codex-relay --bg` alive in a chosen workspace dir; respawn on exit; SIGTERM forward on shutdown so the pairing/auth state stays consistent.
- `com.claudio1.codex-relay.plist` — LaunchAgent (`RunAtLoad` + `KeepAlive`) that runs the supervisor at login.
- Wire both into the existing `install.sh` so one install gets both bridges.

One real constraint to decide before building: codex-relay binds **a single fixed port (8787)**, so unlike the claude supervisor (which spawns one server per `~/dev` subdir), this one is fundamentally single-instance — it should run once, in one workspace dir (most likely `~/dev` itself, since the mobile app pairs to the host, not per-project). That makes the supervisor much simpler than the claude one (no discovery loop, just one child).

Want me to add it now? If yes, two quick choices:

expected.rec_session: remote control dir, Separate script + plist (Recommended)
